paragraphs: Elazar, in charge of the curtain, beginning of Shekalim, chapter 5. [Glosses: Elazar. (a) Rabbi Abba bar Zemina in Rabbi Elazar Ze'ira’s name: so Yuchasin and Tosafot, Shabbat 12, end of b. But this is an error: it should read in Rabbi Ze'ira’s name; Elazar is erroneous, and they did not correct it. See his entry and how many errors occur on this matter in the Talmud and Yuchasin. (b) Sukkah 44b: Ivo said, “I was standing before Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok.” Requires examination; Yuchasin reads before Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak, and the new editions did not correct it. See Seder Tannaim ve-Amoraim under Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok. (c) Horayot 13b: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak; the same subject immediately has son of Rabbi Tzadok. (d) Sanhedrin 14a: “He ordained five elders,” etc., and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon should read Shammua. (e) Semachot, chapter 8: Rabban Gamliel the elder and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah eulogized Shmuel the small. Requires examination: Rabban Gamliel the elder died before Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah was born; they did not correct it. Perhaps R.E.b.A. means Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh. (f) Eruvin 23a, Mishnah: “I heard from Rabbi Elazar” should be Eliezer; the new editions did not correct it. (g) Nazir 56b, end of chapter 7: Rabbi Eliezer says from Rabbi Yehoshua should read Rabbi Elazar, namely Elazar ben Shammua. Examine my proof: in three places in the Gemara, Rashi, and Tosafot, Eliezer should read Elazar; the new editions did not correct it. (h) Eruvin 65b: Rabbi Eliezer asked Rav should read Elazar; likewise Hachovel 87, end of a and b. (i) Rosh Hashanah, chapter 2, 24a, passage: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says, “If it was not seen at its proper time, they do not sanctify it”; Pelimo says, etc.; Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says, “Either way they do not sanctify it,” etc. Thus his statements contradict each other. But see Rashi, Rosh Hashanah 8b, on “and you do not,” etc.: like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, who says below, chapter 2, “Either way they do not sanctify,” etc. Thus 24a is erroneous and should read Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon saying, “Either way,” etc. (j) Ta'anit 4b: “Did Rabbi Yochanan say so? Did not R.A. say the law follows Rabban Gamliel?” There 6, end of a, the same subject has Rav Chisda saying it; perhaps one is erroneous; not corrected. “Did not R.A. say” is an error and should read Elazar, as in the new editions and 10a. They object from Rabbi Elazar to Rabbi Yochanan because Elazar was his student: presumably his teacher Rabbi Yochanan said it, as I wrote in the rules, and as Tosafot, Yoma 4, end of a. The answer is, “Do you set one man against another?” Rabbi Elazar was a student-colleague of Rabbi Yochanan.]
